If plan_pass's scope/skip/mode-cap exclusions drop a target that the applier's own _partition_by_mode_cap did not drop, a legitimately-dispatchable update/delete is recorded failed instead of applied — a behavior change from the legacy loop which dispatched every outbound mutation.

advisory.finding: apply_phase.apply_mutations forwards `ticket_plans` to applier.apply only when `ctx.ticket_plans is not None`, but applier._typed_batch now raises `TypeError("apply() batch form requires ticket_plans")` whenever ticket_plans is None. Because `ticket_plans` is not a declared `_PassContext` field (it is assigned dynamically by run_differs), any pass that reaches apply_mutations without run_differs having populated it will drop the kwarg and abort a previously-legal non-empty outbound persisting batch with TypeError, instead of the old fall-back to the legacy per-mutation loop.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either declare `ticket_plans` on _PassContext with a non-None default and forward it unconditionally, or change the apply_phase guard so a persisting outbound batch always forwards ticket_plans (failing loudly at the producer if run_differs did not populate it) rather than silently dropping the kwarg into a TypeError.
